physicalNotes: Radius 15.013 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 17702: radius 13.762 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 843.922 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.91) and temperature; scaled from the paper's distance, 123.609 pc, to the cluster's, 134.84 pc: at a fixed temperature the radius grows with the distance, so 13.762 x 134.84/123.609 = 15.013 solar radii (luminosity 1004.3) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 10,444,544 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 8392 +/- 4070 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 17702: effective temperature 8392 +/- 4070 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.113) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.

sources.position: Gaia DR3 source 66714384142368256 (Gaia Collaboration 2023, A&A 674, A1), ICRS at epoch J2016.0, from the archived row src/objects/alcyone/source/photometry/gaia-dr3-source.csv; cross-identification HD 23630, HR 1165, HIP 17702: https://simbad.cds.unistra.fr/simbad/sim-id?Ident=Gaia+DR3+66714384142368256
sources.distance: Hunt & Reffert (2023), Improving the open cluster census. II. An all-sky cluster catalogue with Gaia DR3, A&A 673, A114; CDS J/A+A/673/A114, Table 3 (clusters), Melotte_22: dist50 134.84134308 pc, the distance of the Pleiades, of which Alcyone is a member; its own parallax (McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson 2017 adopt 123.609 pc from Gaia DR1 or the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007) is less certain than the cluster's depth (half its members within 2.70 pc of the centre), and the Hipparcos-era parallaxes of the bright Pleiades are the ones the cluster's distance controversy showed biased (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202346285): 134.84134308 +/- 2.7 pc; Gaia DR3 gives this source no parallax (a two-parameter solution)
sources.properMotion: Gaia DR3 source 66714384142368256 is a two-parameter solution with no proper motion; zero is assumed (at 135 pc, 1 mas/yr would be 1 km/s across the sky)
sources.radialVelocity: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 66714384142368256 (quality B), from 2006AstL...32..759G; Gaia DR3 measures none (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2006AstL...32..759G/abstract)
